indexing, misconceptions: 8 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | mis:indexing->ArrayAccessWithParentheses | wrong rule: a(i) accesses element i of an array. | right rule: Array elements are accessed with square brackets, a[i]. | | mis:indexing->ArrayElementNotVariable | wrong rule: An array element a[i] is not a variable, so it cannot be read into directly or used inside another index, as in a[a[i]]. | right rule: Each element a[i] is a variable of the element type and can be used anywhere a variable of that type can, including as an index. | | mis:indexing->ArrayIndexStartsAtOne | wrong rule: The first element of a is a[1]. | right rule: Numbering begins with 0; the first element is a[0]. | | mis:indexing->ArrayRangeInclusive | wrong rule: new int[n] has slots 0 to n, inclusive. | right rule: The slots are 0 to n - 1. | | mis:indexing->ArrayUseScansAllCells | wrong rule: Using an array means every cell must be scanned. | right rule: Arrays allow random access: a[i] reaches one element directly, and a loop visits only the elements the task needs. | | mis:indexing->ElementBoundToOldIndex | wrong rule: After i changes, X[i] still refers to the element at the old value of i. | right rule: a[i] is evaluated with the current value of i each time it is used. | | mis:indexing->ElementNameIsWholeArray | wrong rule: X[i] names the whole array, not one element. | right rule: The array is a; a[i] is the single element at index i. | | mis:indexing->IndexIsValue | wrong rule: i and a[i] are the same thing, so the position is the stored value. | right rule: i is a position; a[i] is the value stored at that position. |
